comments.value:
This has a large downside to it as well. Almost everyone I know is from Europe, Japan, or Korea, while I am from North America. The problem here should be obvious I feel seeing as only around 25% of my friends list is of my own region. You have my sympathy for crashers, but for annoying or disrespectful people you've already said the solution yourself.
It seems obvious - make the choice use the block button. It's very hard to have sympathy when you state that solution then follow it by saying you don't use that solution because 'we don't do that.' Maybe it's time you did. It's a game feature designed for the exact scenarios you describe.
For many people in VRChat the best experiences are those of meeting people who are very different from them. People who are learning languages, people who are studying culture and people, or people who are just interested, would all be hurt by a regional block. I don't feel that it's worth forcing global rifts between people because one region refuses to use a block button.
People have been dealing with this stuff in other regions too. Racism. Harassment. Crashing. Generally unpleasant behavior. It all happens in western regions as well and the people don't like it in these regions either. Just some food for thought.
Most people in the western regions can probably say "90% of hackers/trolls/crashers" are from *certain  countries* let's say because I don't want to get in trouble by saying locations, but nobody asks for those countries to get region blocked from our instances. Once again, we have the block button for a reason and most people from those places aren't like that.

@{614ff9c11daf141e2b9bb1a5|full_name}: I have already stated, most people in East Asian societies do not use the block button, this is simply not the way people tend to approach things. There is expectation that people understand that their behavior is causing trouble for others and that they should stop disrespectful or harassing behavior. 
Understand this instead of telling the society here to use blocking "just because Western societies treat using the block button as expected and normal", there are players that do use the block button but those are far and few between as it is simply not in our societal culture to do so, and if you find that an issue, then flip it around for a moment and consider this- Our societies expect people to discipline themselves and be considerate by nature, be respectful, and leave people who do not wish to interact with them alone, why doesn't the Western playerbase just do that then and fix its issue of being chronically unpleasant?
Are you going to use the same logic regarding the report feature as well? Because players in East Asia also do not commonly use the report feature, not just because of language barriers but because it is, again, not a norm in our areas to go out of our way to report someone, and it is not expected that someone would act in a way that would be generally regarded as uncivilized. 
Unpleasant behavior obviously happens often in the Western side of VRChat, and its players are the main reason for me even asking for such a feature. If you say most of the people you know are from Europe, Korea and Japan, then you should know very well that East Asian players do not tend to exhibit the same behaviors. While generally unpleasant behavior is somewhat of an expected "norm" in the West, this is extremely disliked in Asia and other regions. Most Chinese, Korean, and (especially) Japanese users would be extremely appalled at the behavior displayed by said problematic players.
Our cultures and societies are very much different, and how many are aware of the differences and showing due respect, instead of just going at it with the views of the West? As you've demonstrated with the chiding over a lack of use of the in-game block feature.
My suggestion is to create an option that would fit not just norms in East Asia, but by extension this would also benefit others as there would be additional choice that could be utilized if need be. And of course, this suggestion can be circumvented but it will stop a lot of the general troublemakers. I am not advocating a hard region block or lock, I am advocating for a choice-based, per-instance-based region restriction, and even if this is implemented there will be worlds without said restrictions available.
Meeting different people is not an issue, it is a considerable amount of people from another foreign culture, who have no intention of actually communicating (or just want to shock others), have no due respect, and join in to make the world generally unenjoyable for the players who are already in it. I understand that you meeting different people from various regions, cultures, and walks of life are part of the experience and fun of VRChat, but one should also not underestimate the potential of forced, unwanted interaction to spark conflict.
As I have stated in my original post, the world is not the same, the global rifts you speak of are realities, not artificially created.
Region-blocking is what would be generally accepted as a "block button" solution here in East Asia. People from various regions should also have the right to determine whether they want to interact with foreigners, especially when it comes to the highly different societal cultures and norms of East and West.

This could backfire... while normal people would not be able to join, the bad people would be attracted even more because it's blocked. And skipping regional blocks was never too complicated.
I think VrChat would just need more moderators that could respond to reports in-game and have moderators knowing different languages.

@{5f2dea8d22470972dc58e995|full_name}: The issue of it not being a watertight solution was noted in my proposal. For moderators, the issue would be as earlier noted, players in Asia and potentially players from other regions that are not Europe or the US, usually do not use the report or block function as it is not a norm here. Leaving it to VRChat-end moderation may also be an immense task owing to how often these incidents happen. That being said, more moderators that are from different regions would be helpful to VRChat as a whole.

details:
In VRChat, there is a huge issue regarding Western players harassing players in East Asia and elsewhere. We in Asia who focus on respect, politeness and pleasant behavior, have immense cultural differences with those in the West, and this has led to unpleasant interactions owing to the unwanted presence of Western players―which while not entirely made out of "bad apples", have "bad apples" in very noticeable and considerable numbers―in worlds hosted in East Asia, including disrespectful behavior, racist attacks, harassment, crashing attacks and other forms of uncivilized behavior. It is especially insulting when Western players come into worlds that Japanese users have made and then proceed to commence racist harassment towards East Asian players within those worlds.

Understand that people in East Asia and elsewhere, also have a right to choose who they want to and who they do not want to interact with, and owing to our societal nature here, people do not often bother with blocking or reporting. It is more commonly expected for people to simply leave others alone.

These differences are not something you can resolve just by "talking" as they often are irreconcilable owing to fundamentally different societal natures, language barrier, and a willing lack of understanding or courtesy by Western players, especially when the problematic people in question do not speak reason and only want to ruin the experiences of others. Also understand other people in other regions of the world have immensely different worldviews, and thus just because this suggestion sounds "illiberal" or "restrictive" to someone in the West does not mean it does not have its merits or validity. If VRChat truly wants to become something for "everyone" then it must respect differing worldviews, societal views, and perspectives that different cultures have, not pretend that everyone is somehow the same.

The addition of an instance dependent region blocking feature that can be chosen by the instance creator will allow a general resolution of this issue. If players want to have interactions with people outside of their immediate regions, they can do so, and if they do not want to, they should be able to determine that as well.
title: Instance-choice Region Blocking
